purpose: sparse far-plane atmosphere overlay candidate; alpha allows VDP color 0 to reveal the back color and lower plane
prompt: Produce one wide 3:1 continuous panorama of a moonlit Japanese mountain night. Deliberately sparse, clean hand-authored 16-bit arcade pixel art, as if designed at 320x112 logical resolution and enlarged with nearest-neighbor. Broad stepped pixel clusters and flat solid color regions; each small detail at least 8 logical pixels wide. Five-color role palette only: deep navy sky, dark blue far ridge, royal-blue nearer ridge, muted periwinkle cloud edge, pale ivory moon. The game already has its castle, wall, railing and floor in the near plane, so draw no buildings, architecture, trees, foliage, foreground terrain, ground or water. One moon around 24% of width in upper half; three differently sized asymmetric cloud masses; two distant mountain ridges across the lower third with one broad higher peak toward the right and a low saddle at left. Quiet open sky around the moon. Mountain contour non-repeating across width but fills and cloud forms economical for 8x8 tile reuse. No gradients, antialiasing, airbrush, photorealism, checker dithering, pixel noise, tiny stars, duplicate moon, mirrored halves, repeated mountain pattern, props, text, people, UI, border, or watermark. Restrained low-frequency source plate, not finished game art or a full scene.
